claims.explanation: MG-132 is a reversible proteasome inhibitor whose selectivity likely reflects dependence on proteasome/ubiquitin-proteasome system activity and NF-kB signaling, since proteasome inhibition stabilizes HIF-1alpha, blocks NF-kB activation, and induces stress/apoptotic responses. Lines with high proteasome-pathway or NF-kB dependence, or with mutations causing proteotoxic/ER stress, should be more sensitive, while lines with low proteasome dependence or strong compensatory stress responses should be protected.

features.basis: Proteasome inhibition blocks NF-kB activation; NF-kB-dependent lines may be more affected
NF-kB pathway activation and RELB upregulation in virtual cell response
MG-132 stabilizes HIF-1alpha by blocking its proteasomal degradation
Annotated proteasome target; higher expression may increase dependence
p21 upregulation observed in virtual cell response to MG-132
BAG3 upregulation in virtual cell response, involved in proteostasis
NOXA upregulation in virtual cell response, promotes apoptosis
p53 pathway loss may reduce apoptotic response to proteasome inhibition
CFTR quality control degradation is proteasome-dependent; mutant CFTR may increase proteasome load
TNF-alpha signaling modulated by proteasome inhibition and NF-kB
miR-155 levels controlled by NF-kB and affected by MG-132
miR-125b downregulated by MG-132 and targets NF-kB pathway components
